newsitem.title: USA: Virginia to "retire" racially offensive state song.
newsitem.headline: Virginia to "retire" racially offensive state song.

text.p: The Virginia Senate voted on Tuesday to retire the official state song amid charges that its references to "darkey" and "old massa" were racially offensive.

The Senate voted 24-15 to make "Carry Me Back to Old Virginny" the "official state song emeritus," a compromise for those who wanted the song junked entirely. It also voted to set up a committee to find a new state song.
The motion, proposed by senators Stephen Newman, a white Republican, and Louise Lucas, a black Democrat, must now go to the House of Delegates for final approval.
Debate over the song has raged for several years and it is already no longer played at state functions or schools.
Blacks and many whites bridled at lines like: "There's where the old darkey's heart am longed to go. That's where I laboured so hard for old massa."
Curt Diemer, a spokesman for Newman, told Reuters: "Senator Newman was disturbed that we did not have a song we could sing at schools or political events."
He said those voting against the motion came from different ends of the political spectrum -- blacks who wanted it totally repealed and whites who thought it was a fine song.
An earlier bid to replace the offensive words -- substituting "dreamers" for "darkey" and "my old loved ones" for "massa" -- failed.
"The other problem is that we don't have a good one out there for a new state song," Diemer said.
Some 30 people had sent Newman's office prospective new songs but most were less than inspiring, he said.
"Carry Me Back to Old Virginny" was writtem by a black minstrel, James Bland, in the last century and has been Virginia's state song since 1940.
